name: Spain
tagline: Several countries wearing one flag, with the second-highest average altitude in Europe.
summary: Spain is a high dry plateau with green mountains at the top and a coastline everyone else visits. It carries eight centuries of Islamic rule in its south, a Celtic wet north, and languages that are not dialects of anything. Eating happens late — lunch at two, dinner at ten — and the pace only makes sense once you accept it. The interior, Extremadura, Aragón, Galicia's inland, is nearly empty.

season.note: July and August in the interior are brutal — Córdoba regularly passes 44°C — and the coast is full. May, June, September and October are the real seasons. The green north is best in summer, when everywhere else is unbearable.

getting_around: AVE high-speed rail links Madrid to Barcelona, Seville, Valencia and Málaga in two to three hours; book early. Buses cover the interior where rail does not. Northern Spain needs a car.
food: Tapas, which is a way of eating rather than a dish — and free with a drink in Granada and León
Jamón ibérico de bellota, from pigs that ate acorns, sliced by hand
Regional: paella only in Valencia, pintxos in the Basque country, pulpo in Galicia
know: Lunch runs 14:00–16:00 and kitchens genuinely close; dinner starts at 21:00.
Many museums are free in the last two hours of the day.
The Camino de Santiago is a working pilgrimage with its own etiquette, not a long-distance hiking route.

regions.name: Andalusia
regions.summary: The Moorish south: the Alhambra, three great cities, white villages and the mountains behind them.

cities.name: Granada
cities.summary: The last Moorish city in Spain, under the Sierra Nevada, with the Alhambra above it.
highlights: The Alhambra's Nasrid palaces, booked months ahead and worth every minute
The Albaicín's white lanes and the view from San Nicolás at sunset
Free tapas with every drink, which is a real local law of physics
Skiing and the beach within ninety minutes of each other in March

experiences.name: The Nasrid palaces, on a timed ticket
experiences.summary: Half-hour entry slots, sold out weeks ahead. Take the earliest of the day — the courtyards were designed for low light and few people.

experiences.name: Tapas, the Granada way
experiences.summary: Every drink comes with a plate you did not order and cannot choose; four bars is a dinner.

cities.name: Seville
cities.summary: Orange trees, the world's largest gothic cathedral, and flamenco that belongs to specific families.
highlights: The Real Alcázar, still a working royal palace
The Giralda, a minaret with a cathedral built round it
A flamenco peña rather than a tablao — the difference is everything

experiences.name: Flamenco in a peña
experiences.summary: Members' clubs that admit visitors quietly; no castanets, no stage, and the singing is the part that matters.

cities.name: Córdoba
cities.summary: The largest city in the world in the 10th century, with a mosque-cathedral of 856 columns at its centre.
highlights: The Mezquita, a cathedral inserted into a mosque and both left standing
Patio courtyards, opened to the public each May
The Roman bridge at dawn

cities.name: Ronda
cities.summary: A town split by a 120-metre gorge with an 18th-century bridge across it, in the middle of white-village country.
highlights: The Puente Nuevo, and the path down into the gorge below it
One of Spain's oldest bullrings, whether or not you approve
Serranía de Ronda wine, which nobody exports

cities.name: Cádiz
cities.summary: Possibly the oldest continuously inhabited city in western Europe, on a spit, surrounded by water on three sides.
highlights: La Caleta beach between two castles, in the middle of the old town
Carnival in February, which is the best in mainland Spain
Fried fish sold by weight in paper cones

cities.name: Málaga
cities.summary: A port that spent a decade turning itself into a museum city, with Picasso's birthplace and a Moorish fortress above.
highlights: The Picasso Museum, in the city he left at ten
The Alcazaba and Gibralfaro, walked up in half an hour
Espetos: sardines grilled on a stick over a boat full of sand

regions.name: Catalonia & the East
regions.summary: Barcelona, the Costa Brava's coves, Roman Tarragona and the Pyrenees behind.

cities.name: Barcelona
cities.summary: A Roman city inside a medieval city inside a 19th-century grid, with Gaudí's work scattered across all three.
highlights: The Sagrada Família's interior light, which is the actual point
The Eixample grid and its chamfered corners, a 19th-century plan that worked
Santa Caterina and Sant Antoni markets, where the city shops
Montjuïc's Fundació Miró and the view back over the port

experiences.name: The grid, read as a plan
experiences.summary: Cerdà's 1859 blocks were designed with gardens inside; a few have been reopened, and finding them changes how the city reads.

cities.name: Girona & the Empordà
cities.summary: A walled river city with the widest gothic nave in the world, forty minutes from Barcelona and a fraction of the crowd.
highlights: The Jewish quarter, one of Europe's best preserved
The city walls, walkable, with the Pyrenees on the horizon
Empordà wine and the coves of the northern Costa Brava

experiences.name: The Camí de Ronda coastal path
experiences.summary: A smugglers' and coastguards' path linking coves between Begur and Palamós; it reaches beaches no road does.

cities.name: Valencia
cities.summary: A river turned into a nine-kilometre park, a gothic silk exchange, and the actual home of paella.
highlights: Turia gardens: a flood-diverted riverbed, now the city's spine
La Lonja, a gothic trading hall with twisted stone columns
Paella valenciana, with rabbit and beans and no seafood at all

experiences.name: Paella where the rice grows
experiences.summary: The Albufera lagoon south of the city grows the rice and cooks it over orange wood; lunchtime only, and never in the evening.

cities.name: Tarragona
cities.summary: The Roman capital of Hispania, with an amphitheatre on the beach and an aqueduct in the woods.
highlights: The amphitheatre, looking straight out to sea
Les Ferreres aqueduct, walkable along the top
Human tower competitions, on the UNESCO list, in the surrounding towns

regions.name: Madrid & the Centre
regions.summary: The capital on the meseta, and the walled and imperial cities within an hour of it.

cities.name: Madrid
cities.summary: A high plateau capital with three of the world's great galleries in one kilometre and a nightlife that starts at midnight.
highlights: The Prado's Velázquez and Goya, and the Reina Sofía's Guernica
El Rastro flea market on Sunday morning
Retiro park, and the crystal palace in it
Vermouth at noon, which is a Madrid institution

experiences.name: La hora del vermut
experiences.summary: Sunday, around one, house vermouth on tap with an olive and a siphon of soda — the most Madrid ninety minutes there is.

cities.name: Toledo
cities.summary: A city on a granite outcrop in a river loop, where Christian, Jewish and Muslim Spain were one place for centuries.
highlights: El Greco's Burial of the Count of Orgaz, in the church it was painted for
Synagogues built by Muslim craftsmen for Jewish congregations under Christian kings
The city from the far bank at night

cities.name: Segovia
cities.summary: A Roman aqueduct of 167 arches, built without mortar, running straight through the middle of a working town.
highlights: The aqueduct, 28 metres high, dry-stone, still standing after 2,000 years
The Alcázar on its rock, which Disney is said to have borrowed
Cochinillo, roast suckling pig, carved with a plate

cities.name: Salamanca
cities.summary: A university city since 1218, in sandstone that turns gold at sunset, with two cathedrals joined together.
highlights: The Plaza Mayor, the best in Spain and used as a living room
The frog carved on the university facade, which students must find
Old and new cathedrals sharing a wall, 300 years apart

cities.name: Cuenca
cities.summary: Houses hanging over a gorge on two sides, with an abstract art museum inside them.
highlights: The casas colgadas, cantilevered over a 100-metre drop
Spanish Abstract Art Museum, in the hanging houses themselves
The Serranía de Cuenca's rock formations behind the town

regions.name: Green Spain
regions.summary: The Atlantic north: Basque food, Cantabrian mountains, and Galicia at the end of the pilgrimage.

cities.name: San Sebastián
cities.summary: A shell-shaped bay, a belle époque town, and more Michelin stars per head than anywhere on earth.
highlights: Pintxos bar to pintxos bar in the Parte Vieja, one dish each
La Concha beach and the walk round to Ondarreta
Cider houses inland in Astigarraga, January to April

experiences.name: A pintxo crawl, done properly
experiences.summary: One drink and one signature dish per bar, standing, then move. Sitting down is how visitors get it wrong.

cities.name: Santiago de Compostela
cities.summary: The end of the Camino: a granite city that rains constantly and fills each afternoon with people who have walked there.
highlights: The pilgrims' mass, and the botafumeiro when it swings
Arriving on foot into the Praza do Obradoiro
Galician seafood at the Mercado de Abastos

experiences.name: The last hundred kilometres
experiences.summary: From Sarria, five days, and the minimum distance for a compostela. Busy, sociable, and still the real thing.

cities.name: Picos de Europa (Cangas de Onís)
cities.summary: Limestone peaks twenty kilometres from the sea, with a cable car, gorges and blue cheese aged in caves.
highlights: The Cares gorge, twelve kilometres cut into a cliff
Cabrales cheese, matured in mountain caves
Covadonga's lakes and the shrine below them

cities.name: Bilbao
cities.summary: A steel city that commissioned one building in 1997 and changed what cities thought was possible.
highlights: The Guggenheim, and the argument about whether one building can do that
Pintxos in the Casco Viejo, standing, one per bar
The Vizcaya transporter bridge, from 1893 and still carrying cars

experiences.name: Across on the hanging gondola
experiences.summary: The world's oldest transporter bridge, on the UNESCO list, still running every eight minutes as a local crossing.

cities.name: Ribeira Sacra
cities.summary: Vineyards on canyon walls above the Sil, worked from boats and by hand, with Romanesque monasteries in the woods.
highlights: Terraces at gradients that need a winch, above a 500-metre gorge
Mencía reds from vines nobody can mechanise
Catamarans up the canyon, and eighteen Romanesque churches within an hour

experiences.name: Heroic viticulture, from the river
experiences.summary: The growers call it viticultura heroica without irony: everything is carried up and down by hand or cable, and the boat is the only way to see why.

regions.name: Aragón & the Pyrenees
regions.summary: Mudéjar brick towers, a Spanish Grand Canyon, and the emptiest inhabited country in Europe.

cities.name: Zaragoza
cities.summary: Roman, Moorish, Christian and industrial in the same city, with a basilica the size of a cathedral on the Ebro.
highlights: The Aljafería, an 11th-century Moorish palace, now the regional parliament
Basílica del Pilar's eleven domes on the river
Mudéjar brickwork, on the UNESCO list, all over the old town

cities.name: Torla & Ordesa
cities.summary: A stone village at the mouth of a glacial canyon, under the third-highest peak in the Pyrenees.
highlights: Ordesa canyon and the Cola de Caballo, a full day on a good path
Monte Perdido, 3,355 metres, and the bearded vultures over it
A shuttle bus in summer because the valley road is closed to cars

cities.name: Albarracín
cities.summary: A pink town wrapped in a river bend and a wall that climbs the ridge above it, in one of Europe's emptiest provinces.
highlights: The wall walk, up the hill and back down
Prehistoric rock shelters in the pine woods outside
A province with fewer than ten people per square kilometre

regions.name: The Balearic Islands
regions.summary: Four islands with four different characters: a gothic cathedral on one, prehistoric stone on another, and a mountain range that walks well in winter.

cities.name: Palma de Mallorca
cities.summary: A cathedral with a Gaudí interior on the harbour, and the Tramuntana mountains behind it for the other three seasons.
highlights: La Seu, whose canopy Gaudí redesigned and whose chapel Barceló repainted in 2007
The Serra de Tramuntana, UNESCO-listed, and best from October to May
The wooden train to Sóller, running since 1912

experiences.name: The wooden train to Sóller
experiences.summary: 1912 rolling stock through thirteen tunnels and an orange valley, then a tram to the port. Ordinary transport, and the best hour on the island.

cities.name: Ciutadella, Menorca
cities.summary: Menorca's old capital: a sandstone harbour town on an island that is a UNESCO biosphere reserve and mostly farmland.
highlights: Camí de Cavalls: 185 km of bridle path round the whole coast
Talayotic stone monuments, on the UNESCO list since 2023
Beaches on the north coast reached only on foot

regions.name: Extremadura
regions.summary: The far west: Roman theatres still in use, conquistador palaces, black pigs under oak trees, and almost no visitors.

cities.name: Cáceres
cities.summary: A walled old town of Moorish towers and conquistador palaces, with storks nesting on most of them.
highlights: A UNESCO old town with no modern buildings inside the walls at all
Storks on every tower from February
Ibérico ham from acorn-fed pigs in the dehesa outside

cities.name: Mérida
cities.summary: The best Roman ruins in Spain, including a theatre that still stages classical drama every summer.
highlights: The theatre, from 15 BC, with a summer festival on its stage
A 792-metre Roman bridge, still walked across
The national museum of Roman art, in a Rafael Moneo building

experiences.name: Classical drama in a Roman theatre
experiences.summary: Greek and Roman plays staged every July and August in the theatre they were written for, which is a different experience from reading them.
